justification: Closes a forgery/mislabel vector in the PDF report. On a cache hit generate_conveyancing_pdf rendered the cached property's data but took the address label (and the address-derived lookups: shadow, structures, former-council) from req.address, so a caller could pair a valid report_id for a clean property with a different property's address and produce a due-diligence PDF showing one property's data under another's address. The label and all address-derived work now use a single bound `address` that comes from the cache on a hit and from req.address only on a miss (the resolution key). A cache entry lacking its own address (or coordinates) is treated as a miss and fully re-resolved, so no caller-supplied address is ever paired with cached data.

pre_impl.existing_data: Uses the existing pipeline cache written by run_conveyancing's _save_pipeline_cache, which already stores address, prop_id, lat, lng and lot_wkt together. No new data source, query, or fetcher is introduced.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Confirmed all req.address uses in generate_conveyancing_pdf (previously at strata, former-council, shadow, structures, the generate_pdf label and the response) are within this one handler; run_conveyancing and _resolve_property keep their own req.address uses, so no blanket rename was possible and each site was rebound individually.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: a single bound local `address` for the whole handler and the cache-hit guard now also requiring a cached address. Deliberately unchanged: the cache-hit unpacking of controls/valuation/overlays, the coordinate binding from #818, and _resolve_property.

functions.name: generate_conveyancing_pdf
functions.input: a ConveyancingPdfRequest; on a cache hit the address label and address-derived lookups come from the cached entry, on a miss from req.address (the same key _resolve_property resolves)
functions.output: a PDF whose address label, shadow, structures and former-council lookups all describe the one resolved/cached property; the caller's address never labels cached data from a different property
functions.if_none: a cache entry lacking its own address or coordinates is treated as a miss and fully re-resolved via _resolve_property (which raises 422 on an unresolvable address, 503 on a resolver outage)

values: N/A - reads no DB or API values directly; wraps the existing pipeline cache and _resolve_property.
queries: N/A - no SQL is written or changed in this diff.

break_it.scenario: A caller runs a report on a clean property, keeps its report_id, then requests the PDF with that report_id but a different (problematic) property's address.
break_it.what_happens: The old handler rendered the clean property's cached controls, valuation and hazards but labelled the PDF with the problematic property's address, forging a due-diligence document for the wrong property.
break_it.how: On a cache hit the address label and address-derived lookups come from cached['address'], not req.address, so the report_id always renders its own property fully.

break_it.scenario: A legacy cache entry for report_id A has coordinates but no stored address, and a caller supplies property B's address.
break_it.what_happens: An earlier version of this fix coalesced address = cached.get('address') or req.address, so a missing cached address silently restored the mix-up: A's data labelled with B's address.
break_it.how: The cache-hit guard now also requires cached.get('address'); an entry missing it falls through to full authoritative re-resolution rather than borrowing the caller's address.

break_it.scenario: A future edit passes req.address to a new fetcher, the PDF label, or the response instead of the bound address.
break_it.what_happens: That path would render or query for the caller's address while the rest of the PDF describes the cached property, reintroducing the mislabel for that data source.
break_it.how: An AST guard asserts every req.address in the handler is the right-hand side of an `address = ...` binding and that generate_pdf is labelled with the bound address; a direct use fails the test.
